items.title: [Bug]: Generated skills cannot be inspected or located from the macOS app UI
items.body:
## Bug Description

When Hermes creates a new skill from the macOS app's self-improvement review flow, the user is notified that the skill was created, but there does not appear to be any way to inspect, open, edit, or locate the skill afterward from the app UI.

This is a visibility and trust problem: the app has created a durable behavior-affecting artifact, but the user cannot see what was written, where it was stored, or what the skill will do when enabled.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use the Hermes macOS app in a normal chat session.
2. End or complete a session where the self-improvement review creates a skill.
3. Observe the message:
   `Self-improvement review: Skill 'software-development-orchestration' created.`
4. Try to click that message to inspect the newly created skill.
5. Open `Skills & Tools`.
6. Search for `software-development-orchestration`.
7. Observe that the skill appears in the list with a description and an on/off toggle.

## Expected Behavior

Hermes should provide a clear inspection path for a newly created skill. At minimum, one or more of these should be available:

- The "Skill created" message should be clickable and open the skill details.
- The `Skills & Tools` list item should be clickable.
- The skill details view should show the skill body, source/path, category, enabled state, created/updated metadata, and any validation status.
- There should be actions such as `Open`, `Reveal in Finder`, `Edit`, `Disable`, and possibly `Delete`.
- If Hermes intentionally hides editing, it should still expose a read-only details view and the filesystem location.

## Actual Behavior

The creation message is not clickable.

The skill can be found from `Skills & Tools` by searching for `software-development-orchestration`, but the visible UI only appears to expose an enable/disable toggle. There is no obvious way to:

- open the skill,
- inspect the skill instructions,
- edit it,
- reveal where it was saved,
- understand why it was created,
- or verify what behavior the enabled skill will affect.

## Why This Matters

Skills are not just passive UI entries; they can change future agent behavior. If Hermes can create skills automatically but the app only exposes a toggle afterward, users are left blind to:

- what behavior was persisted,
- whether the skill contains an incorrect or over-broad lesson,
- whether the skill should be trusted,
- where to inspect or back it up,
- and how to correct it if it is wrong.

This is especially concerning for self-improvement flows because the created artifact is derived from a session-specific experience. Users need transparency before keeping that skill enabled.

## Affected Component

- Skills (skill loading, skill hub, skill guard)
- macOS app / `Skills & Tools` UI
- Self-improvement review flow

## Operating System

macOS, using the Hermes macOS app.

## Hermes Version

Unknown from the visible UI during this report.

## Debug Report

Not available. This report is based on the visible macOS app behavior.

## Proposed Fix

Add an inspectable skill details path in the macOS app:

1. Make the "Skill created" toast/status message link directly to the created skill.
2. Make each skill row in `Skills & Tools` clickable, not just toggleable.
3. Show the full skill content and metadata in a details pane.
4. Include the on-disk path or a `Reveal in Finder` action.
5. Add edit/delete controls if those operations are supported; otherwise make the details view explicitly read-only.
6. Consider adding a post-creation review state so newly generated skills can be reviewed before being enabled by default.

## Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

items.title: fix(telegram): pipe table auto-rich bypasses rich_messages: false config

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
## Bug Description

Commit `9d225fbf4` (fix(telegram): auto-rich pipe tables and topic routing for sendRichMessage) added `_content_is_pipe_table_primary()` which forces pipe-table content through `sendRichMessage` **even when `rich_messages: false`** is configured.

This reintroduces the "This message is not supported on your version of Telegram" error on clients that don't support Bot API 10.1 rich messages (AyuGram, Telegram Web, some desktop clients).

## Root Cause

`_rich_delivery_enabled()` was changed to:

```python
def _rich_delivery_enabled(self, content: str) -> bool:
    return bool(
        getattr(self, "_rich_messages_enabled", True)
        or self._content_is_pipe_table_primary(content)  # ← bypasses config
    )
```

The `or` clause means pipe tables always go through `sendRichMessage` regardless of the `rich_messages` opt-in setting.

## Expected Behavior

When `platforms.telegram.extra.rich_messages: false` is set, **no** content should be sent via `sendRichMessage` — including pipe tables. The legacy MarkdownV2 path should be used for all content.

## Actual Behavior

Pipe tables are auto-routed to `sendRichMessage` even with `rich_messages: false`, breaking delivery on AyuGram and Telegram Web.

## Fix

Remove the `or self._content_is_pipe_table_primary(content)` bypass from `_rich_delivery_enabled()` so the config flag is fully respected.

```python
def _rich_delivery_enabled(self, content: str) -> bool:
    return bool(
        getattr(self, "_rich_messages_enabled", True)
    )
```

## Related

- Fixes #46098, #45785 (original reports, still open)
- Regression from `9d225fbf4` which landed after #50322 (the opt-in fix)
- PR #48422 addresses the same config default but doesn't cover the pipe table bypass

### Bug Description

When USER.md or MEMORY.md contains bytes outside valid UTF-8, the memory tool fails with a decode error like: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xd1 in position ... invalid continuation byte. This appears to come from path.read_text(encoding="utf-8") in the memory path, with no fallback or error handling. Once it hits, memory writes fail entirely and the agent can no longer save or update memory for that profile. In our case it also caused cascading failures in the Photon/iMessage send pipeline after the memory write failed.

Expected: invalid bytes should be handled gracefully (e.g. errors="replace"), or at minimum should not block all future tool use.

Suggested fix: use path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"), or validate/sanitize content before writing.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Have a non-UTF-8 byte get written into USER.md or MEMORY.md (e.g. from a smart quote/dash saved with an encoding mismatch)
2. Attempt any memory_tool save afterward
3. Crash: UnicodeDecodeError in memory_tool.py, _read_file → _reload_target → add

### Expected Behavior

Invalid legacy bytes should be handled gracefully (e.g. replace with the standard UTF-8 replacement character). At minimum, the error should not prevent further tool use.

Suggested fix: use path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"), or detect/sanitize encoding defensively before loading memory files.

### Actual Behavior

Memory tool save crashes with: UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xd1 in position 219: invalid continuation byte

Traceback path: memory_tool.py line 639 (_read_file) → line 268 (_reload_target) → line 318 (add) → line 964 (memory_tool)

After this, all memory saves failed, and the Photon/iMessage send pipeline also failed with a separate but related error (sidecar returned 500, internal sidecar error) while trying to deliver a response during the same broken session.

Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)

macOS (Sequoia/Sonoma — whatever version, check with: sw_vers -productVersion if unsure)

The crash originates in tools/memory_tool.py line 639, _read_file(), which calls path.read_text(encoding="utf-8") with no error handling. A single invalid byte in USER.md or MEMORY.md causes every subsequent memory read/write to fail.

items.title: [MoA]: Default auxiliary timeout of 600s makes MoA 5-10× slower than necessary

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Summary

The default `auxiliary.moa_reference.timeout` and `auxiliary.moa_aggregator.timeout` are both **600 seconds (10 minutes)**. This causes MoA tasks to take 5-10× longer than necessary, because:

- Each MoA turn runs references in parallel + aggregator sequentially
- A task with 4 tool calls = 5 MoA phases = potentially 15 API calls
- With 600s timeout, a single slow API call can stall the entire phase for 10 minutes

## Real-world reproduction

**Setup:**
```yaml
moa:
  presets:
    go-moa:
      reference_models:
        - provider: opencode-go
          model: glm-5.2
        - provider: opencode-go
          model: deepseek-v4-pro
      aggregator:
        provider: opencode-go
        model: deepseek-v4-pro
```

**Task:** Create a creative portfolio HTML page (single file, vanilla HTML+CSS+JS)

**Results:**
- **Expected:** ~8-12 minutes (5 phases × ~120s each)
- **Actual:** **31 minutes 46 seconds** (5 phases with slow API calls dragging to near-timeout)

**Fix applied:**
```yaml
auxiliary:
  moa_reference:
    timeout: 120   # was 600
  moa_aggregator:
    timeout: 180   # was 600
```

After fix, estimated latency drops to ~8-12 minutes (still slow but no longer absurd).

## Proposed changes

1. **Lower the default timeout** from 600s to 120s for `moa_reference` and 180s for `moa_aggregator` in `hermes_cli/config.py` DEFAULT_CONFIG
2. **Or make it provider-aware** — opencode-go models typically respond in 30-90s; 120s is generous
3. **Document the timeout behavior** in the MoA docs page and the config reference
4. **Consider per-preset timeout overrides** so different presets can have different timeouts based on their providers

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.17.0 (2026.6.19)
- Provider: opencode-go
- Models: glm-5.2, deepseek-v4-pro
- Platform: Termux/Android

Body:
Discord voice channel input (STT pipeline) crashes every time on Linux with:

NameError: name 'windows_hide_flags' is not defined

Location: plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py, line 682, inside the
pcm_to_wav function's subprocess.run() call:

    creationflags=windows_hide_flags(),

`windows_hide_flags()` appears to be a Windows-only helper (presumably for
suppressing a console window flash) that is either not imported or not
defined when running on Linux. Every voice message triggers this crash,
so Discord voice input never reaches Whisper/STT.

Full traceback:
  File ".../discord/adapter.py", line 2707, in _process_voice_input
    await asyncio.to_thread(VoiceReceiver.pcm_to_wav, pcm_data, wav_path)
  File ".../discord/adapter.py", line 682, in pcm_to_wav
    creationflags=windows_hide_flags(),
NameError: name 'windows_hide_flags' is not defined

Environment: Linux (Ubuntu 24.04, ARM64/aarch64), official Docker image
nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest

Workaround that resolves it: remove the `creationflags=windows_hide_flags()`
line entirely (or guard it behind `if sys.platform == "win32"`), since
`subprocess.run` works fine without it on Linux.

items.title: hermes plugins enable/list can't see pip-installed (entry-point) plugins, though the runtime loads them

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Summary

The plugin CLI (`hermes plugins list` / `enable` / `setup`) discovers plugins only from **directories** — bundled `<repo>/plugins/` and `~/.hermes/plugins/`. It never enumerates the `hermes_agent.plugins` entry-point group. The runtime `PluginManager`, however, **does** scan that group. So a pip-installed plugin loads fine at gateway runtime, yet `hermes plugins enable <name>` reports it as "not installed or bundled" and it never shows up in `hermes plugins list`.

Since a plugin only loads when its key is in `plugins.enabled` (config.yaml), and the CLI is what writes that key — but refuses for plugins it can't see — the documented pip-install path can't be enabled through the CLI at all. The only workaround is hand-editing `~/.hermes/config.yaml`.

## Where

- Runtime loader **does** scan entry points: `hermes_cli/plugins.py` — `PluginManager.discover_and_load` step 4 calls `_scan_entry_points()`, which reads the `hermes_agent.plugins` group (`ENTRY_POINTS_GROUP = "hermes_agent.plugins"`).
- CLI discovery **does not**: `hermes_cli/plugins_cmd.py` — `_discover_all_plugins()` only walks `get_bundled_plugins_dir()` and `_plugins_dir()` (`~/.hermes/plugins/`); there is no entry-point enumeration. `cmd_list`, the `enable` command, and `setup` all build on it.

## Repro

```sh
pip install your-hermes-plugin        # a package exposing a hermes_agent.plugins entry point
hermes plugins list                   # plugin is absent
hermes plugins enable your-plugin     # "Plugin 'your-plugin' is not installed or bundled."
```

Yet at gateway runtime the same package is discovered and loaded via its entry point — once its key is added to `plugins.enabled` by hand.

## Expected

`hermes plugins list` / `enable` / `setup` should see entry-point plugins too, matching the runtime loader, so a pip-installed plugin can be enabled through the CLI like any directory plugin.

## Suggested fix

Have `_discover_all_plugins()` also enumerate the `hermes_agent.plugins` entry-point group (e.g. reuse `PluginManager._scan_entry_points`, or share a single discovery path between the CLI and the loader so the two can't drift). Each entry-point plugin would surface with a `source: "pip"` and a null directory path.

---

_Issue AI-generated, human-reviewed._

items.title: v0.17.0 Renderer stuck in fontations+temporal_rs loop — GPU 98% active, 13W sustained power draw

labels.name: area/usage-cost
labels.description: Token accounting, usage reporting, billing, cost tracking

items.body:
## Summary

Since updating to **v0.17.0** (build Jun 27, 2026), the Hermes desktop app's Electron Renderer process enters a continuous `fontations` + `temporal_rs` rendering loop that keeps the GPU at ~98% active residency and draws ~13W sustained — roughly **4x the normal idle power**. The issue reproduces immediately on every launch and persists indefinitely.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| **Hermes** | v0.17.0 (desktop app) |
| **Electron** | 40.10.2 |
| **macOS** | 26.2 (25C56) |
| **Chip** | Apple M4 |
| **Displays** | 2 displays: 4K (3840x2160, main) + vertical (1800x3200) |

## Symptoms

### Power metrics (`sudo powermetrics --samplers cpu_power,gpu_power -n 1 -i 3000`)

```
CPU Power: 5703 mW
GPU Power: 13501 mW       <- normal idle: <1000 mW
ANE Power: 0 mW
Combined Power: 19204 mW   <- normal idle: 3000-5000 mW

GPU HW active residency:  96.50%  (1578 MHz: 96%)
GPU idle residency:        3.50%
```

### Top processes (`ps -Arc -o pid,pcpu,comm -r`)

```
PID   %CPU  COMM
166   62.6  WindowServer
719   45.6  Hermes Helper (Renderer)
709   33.6  Hermes Helper (GPU)
```

### WindowServer call graph (`sudo sample <WindowServer_pid> 3`)

WindowServer spends ~100% of its time in the Metal compositor, driven by Hermes continuous invalidation:

```
2206 update_display_callback -> CGXUpdateDisplay -> WS::Updater::UpdateDisplays
  -> 468 SLCADisplay::render_update -> CompositorMetal::CompositeLayersToDestination
       -> 464 MetalCompositeLayers -> MetalCompositeLayer
            -> 446 CARenderOGLRenderDisplayWithOptions -> CA::OGL::render
                 -> 381 render_prepared_layers -> render_layers (recursive, 4+ levels deep)
```

### Hermes Renderer call graph (`sudo sample <Renderer_pid> 3`)

The renderer is stuck in a tight loop between Chromium new **Fontations** font engine (Rust-based, `fontations_ffi`) and the **Temporal** API (`temporal_rs`), both compiled into the Electron Framework:

```
2327 main-thread
  -> 2327 ElectronMain -> uv_run -> node event loop
       -> 1887 mach_msg (blocking on GPU compositor IPC)
       ->  433 temporal_rs_OwnedRelativeTo_empty
            -> 420 temporal_rs_PlainTime_second
                 -> 390 fontations_ffi$font_ref_is_valid
                      -> 229 fontations_ffi$font_ref_is_valid (deep recursion)
                           -> temporal_rs_ZonedDateTime_offset_nanoseconds
                                -> temporal_rs_ZonedDateTime_calendar (recursive)
```

The pattern suggests a UI component rendering time/timestamp text via the Temporal API at 60fps, with Fontations re-rasterizing the glyphs every frame.

### Hermes GPU process call graph

The GPU helper is also dominated by `fontations_ffi$font_ref_is_valid` (2454 samples), confirming the font rendering pipeline is the bottleneck:

```
2454 fontations_ffi$font_ref_is_valid
  -> ... -> renderCommandEncoderWithDescriptor (Metal command encoding)
```

## Root Cause Analysis

1. **`fontations_ffi`** - Chromium new Rust-based font engine (replacing FreeType). In Electron 40+, this is the default on Apple Silicon.
2. **`temporal_rs`** - Rust implementation of the JavaScript Temporal API (stage 3 proposal). The renderer is calling Temporal `ZonedDateTime` / `PlainTime` methods in a tight loop, likely formatting timestamps for display.
3. **`--disable-background-timer-throttling`** - Hermes launches with this flag, so the render loop runs at full speed even when the window is not focused/visible.

The combination means some timestamp-rendering UI element (clock, message timestamps, streaming status indicator) triggers a full re-layout and glyph re-rasterization via Fontations on every animation frame, and the background timer throttle is disabled so it never slows down.

## Reproduction

1. Launch Hermes v0.17.0 on Apple Silicon with dual displays
2. Wait 10 seconds for renderer to settle
3. Observe GPU power via `sudo powermetrics --samplers gpu_power -n 1 -i 3000`

## Verification

- **Kill + respawn test**: Killed both Helper processes (`kill 719 709`). Electron auto-respawned new helpers (PID 3704/3686) which immediately re-entered the same loop (59.6% CPU within 8 seconds). This is not a stale/corrupted state - it reproduces on every launch.
- **GPU power before kill**: 13.5W -> **after kill+respawn**: 13.0W (no improvement)

## Impact

- **+10-15W sustained** power draw vs. normal idle (19W combined vs 3-5W)
- WindowServer at 62% CPU degrades entire system responsiveness
- Fan noise, thermal impact on MacBook/Mini with sustained load
- Started with v0.17.0 (Jun 27 build); previous versions did not exhibit this

## Suggested Investigation

1. Identify which renderer-side component calls Temporal APIs in a render loop (likely a clock/timestamp display with `requestAnimationFrame` or short `setInterval`)
2. Check if Fontations glyph caching is failing - the same timestamp string should not re-rasterize every frame
3. Consider whether `--disable-background-timer-throttling` can be scoped (e.g., only for the main process, not all renderer processes)

## Workaround

None found yet - killing and restarting the helpers does not help. The only mitigation is quitting Hermes entirely, which drops GPU power to ~0.5W.

items.title: feat(moa): allow reference slots to set reasoning_effort

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Feature Description

Allow Mixture-of-Agents (MoA) reference model slots to specify a per-slot `reasoning_effort`, e.g.:

```yaml
moa:
  presets:
    default:
      reference_models:
        - provider: openai-codex
          model: gpt-5.5
          reasoning_effort: xhigh
        - provider: openrouter
          model: deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
      aggregator:
        provider: openrouter
        model: anthropic/claude-opus-4.8
```

## Motivation

Hermes already supports session-level `/reasoning <none|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh>` for the acting model. In MoA mode, however, the acting model is the aggregator. Reference models are invoked separately through the MoA runtime, so a user cannot currently make one reference model think harder without also changing the acting/aggregator model behavior.

This is useful for MoA presets where one expert should be high-effort (for example `openai-codex:gpt-5.5` on security/code review) while other references remain at their defaults for latency/cost.

## Proposed Solution

- Preserve optional `reasoning_effort` metadata on MoA model slots during config normalization.
- Validate the value against Hermes/OpenAI-supported levels: `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`.
- Forward reference slot effort as `extra_body={"reasoning": {"effort": ...}}` to `call_llm`, letting the existing provider/transport path translate it to the backend wire format.

## Notes

This is intentionally narrower than general reasoning support: `/reasoning` already exists. The feature is specifically about per-reference overrides inside MoA presets.

## 漏洞描述

`npm run build` 通过 `apps/desktop/scripts/bundle-electron-main.mjs` 把 `apps/desktop/electron/main.cjs` 打成 bundle，然后用 `renameSync` 把 bundle **原地回写到源文件**，污染工作树。原本可读的 7532 行源文件被替换为 14716 行的 minified bundle，无 sourcemap、`git diff` 不可读、源不可维护，需要 `git checkout` 才能恢复。

任何在本地跑过 `npm run build` 的开发者，下一次 `git status` 都会看到 `apps/desktop/electron/main.cjs` 多出约 7000 行修改。

## 繁殖步骤

1. Clone `NousResearch/hermes-agent`
2. `cd apps/desktop && npm install`
3. `npm run build`
4. `cd ../..`
5. `git status` → `apps/desktop/electron/main.cjs` 显示 ~7000 行 modified
6. `head -3 apps/desktop/electron/main.cjs` → 输出 esbuild CJS shim 样板（`__create` / `__defProp` / `__getOwnPropDesc` 等），不再是 `const { app, BrowserWindow, ... }`

## 预期行为

`npm run build` 之后 `git status` 干净，`apps/desktop/electron/main.cjs` 保持原始可读源文件不变。bundle 产物作为打包 artifact 单独存在（如 `electron/main.bundled.cjs`），不覆盖源。

## 实际行为

`apps/desktop/scripts/bundle-electron-main.mjs` 第 17 行 + 第 31 行：

```js
const tmp = resolve(root, 'electron/main.bundled.cjs')  // L17
// ...
renameSync(tmp, entry)  // L31 — overwrites electron/main.cjs with the bundle
```

`renameSync` 把 esbuild 的输出重命名到 `electron/main.cjs`（即 `entry`），源被替换为 minified bundle。

## 受影响的组成部分

- `apps/desktop/scripts/bundle-electron-main.mjs`（line 17, 31）
- `apps/desktop/electron/main.cjs`（被覆盖）
- `apps/desktop/package.json`（build 脚本间接触发）

不属于消息平台适配器范畴，与网关无关。

## 调试报告

Report       https://paste.rs/DwQjL
agent.log    https://paste.rs/Qm4xa
gateway.log  https://paste.rs/yy4b7
gui.log      https://paste.rs/J0a0L
desktop.log  https://paste.rs/s7O28

## 操作系统

Windows 10

## Python 版本

3.11.7

## 赫尔墨斯版本

当前本地 HEAD = `28ed88395`，`hermes version` 输出通过上方 `debug share` Report 链接可见。

## 根本原因分析

`apps/desktop/scripts/bundle-electron-main.mjs` 把 bundle 当成"中转产物"处理（先写 `electron/main.bundled.cjs` 再 `renameSync` 回源），意图似乎是用单文件覆盖的方式让 `electron-builder` 直接打 `electron/main.cjs`。但这破坏了开发者工作树，并且没有任何 `.gitignore` 把临时输出排除。

副作用：
- `preload.cjs` 仍单独存在（Electron 用 `path.join(__dirname, 'preload.cjs')` 加载），不受影响
- 任何后续对源 `main.cjs` 的修改/PR 都会被这次覆盖污染掉，无法 review
- 这个污染是 **silent 的**（脚本无警告、无回滚机制），只在 build 中断或后续 `git status` 时才被发现

仓库的 `engines` 要求 `node >= 20`，但脚本里只有 `renameSync` 一行有 `import { renameSync } from 'node:fs'`，去掉该 import + `renameSync` 调用即可让脚本不再污染源。

## 拟议修复

把 bundle 写到 sibling 文件，永远不覆盖源。两种可行方案：

### Option A（最小改动 — 单行语义变化）

```diff
--- a/apps/desktop/scripts/bundle-electron-main.mjs
+++ b/apps/desktop/scripts/bundle-electron-main.mjs
@@ -9,7 +9,6 @@
 import { build } from 'esbuild'
 import { resolve, dirname } from 'node:path'
 import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'
-import { renameSync } from 'node:fs'
 
 const here = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))
 const root = resolve(here, '..')
 const entry = resolve(root, 'electron/main.cjs')
-const tmp = resolve(root, 'electron/main.bundled.cjs')
+const out = resolve(root, 'electron/main.bundled.cjs')
 
 await build({
   entryPoints: [entry],
@@ -25,9 +24,5 @@
   external: ['electron', 'node-pty'],
   logLevel: 'info'
 })
 
-// Overwrite the original with the bundled version.
-renameSync(tmp, entry)
-
-console.log(`bundled ${entry}`)
+console.log(`bundled ${out}`)
```

`package.json` `"main"` 字段改为指向 `electron/main.bundled.cjs`，或在 `electron-builder` 配置中通过 `extraMetadata.main` 指向 bundled（dev 路径继续用源 `main.cjs`）。

### Option B（更清晰的 dev/release 分离）

- `bundle-electron-main.mjs` 输出到 `electron/main.bundled.cjs`，不动源
- `package.json` `"main": "electron/main.cjs"` 保持不变（dev 直接跑源，不需要 bundle）
- `apps/desktop/package.json` `build` 字段新增：
  ```json
  "build": {
    "extraMetadata": {
      "main": "electron/main.bundled.cjs"
    }
  }
  ```
  让 `electron-builder` 打包时用 bundled，本地 dev 不受影响
- 根 `.gitignore` 追加：
  ```
  apps/desktop/electron/main.bundled.cjs
  ```

**验收标准**：
- [ ] `npm run build` 后 `git status` 不显示 `apps/desktop/electron/main.cjs` 有任何改动
- [ ] `apps/desktop/electron/main.cjs` 仍是可读的 7532 行源文件
- [ ] `npm run dev` 仍能正常启动 Electron
- [ ] `npm run dist:win`（或对应平台）仍能打包出可用应用

items.body:
## Bug Description

On Windows 10, opening Hermes Desktop causes black command-line windows (`PseudoConsoleWindow`) to repeatedly flash on screen. The windows appear as normal-sized console windows in the taskbar, lasting < 1 second each, and occur every 10-15 seconds intermittently.

## Root Cause

`hermes_cli/copilot_auth.py` → `_try_gh_cli_token()` calls `subprocess.run(["gh", "auth", "token"])` **without `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` on Windows**. The `gh.exe` CLI uses ConPTY internally, which creates a visible `PseudoConsoleWindow` every time it runs.

This function is called indirectly via:
1. `resolve_copilot_token()` → `_try_gh_cli_token()`
2. `resolve_api_key_provider_credentials("copilot")` in `auth.py:567`
3. `_resolve_api_key_provider()` in `agent/auxiliary_client.py:1621` — iterates `PROVIDER_REGISTRY` for every auxiliary component with `provider: auto` (vision, compression, title_generation, etc.)

Since auxiliary clients are initialized frequently, `gh auth token` is called repeatedly, causing the flickering.

## Environment

- **OS**: Windows 10
- **Hermes**: built from `main` (commit `a590c5e`)
- **gh CLI**: installed at `C:\Program Files\GitHub CLI\gh.EXE`
- **Config**: No copilot provider configured; auxiliary providers set to `provider: auto`

## Fix

In `hermes_cli/copilot_auth.py`, add `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` creation flag on Windows:

```python
# Before (line 138)
result = subprocess.run(
    cmd,
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    timeout=5,
    env=clean_env,
)

# After
sp_kwargs = dict(
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    timeout=5,
    env=clean_env,
)
if sys.platform == "win32":
    sp_kwargs["creationflags"] = subprocess.CREATE_NO_WINDOW
result = subprocess.run(cmd, **sp_kwargs)
```

The same issue likely exists in other `subprocess.run` / `subprocess.Popen` calls across the codebase on Windows. A more comprehensive fix would be to add a helper function (e.g. `_run_hidden()`) that automatically applies `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` on Windows, and audit all subprocess calls.

## Verification

- Ran a 50ms-interval Win32 `EnumWindows` poll targeting `PseudoConsoleWindow` class for 45 seconds
- **Before fix**: 6-8 visible PseudoConsoleWindow detections, all associated with `gh.exe PID=<n>` parented by `pythonw.exe` (`hermes_cli.main dashboard`)
- **After fix**: 0 detections over 45 seconds

## Additional Note

`hermes_cli/doctor.py:2196` has the same missing flag for `gh auth status`, but it only runs on demand via `hermes doctor`, so impact is lower.

## Bug Description

The Hermes Desktop chat UI constantly "flashes" or re-renders every ~10-15 seconds. Typing is interrupted because the input box resets during the flash.

## Root Cause

The Electron frontend keeps losing its WebSocket connection to the Python backend and immediately reconnecting, causing a full UI re-render each cycle.

## Log Evidence (gui.log)

The WebSocket reconnection loop pattern repeats continuously:

```
ws accepted peer=127.0.0.1:XXXXX
ws send failed (WebSocketDisconnect)
ws ready frame send failed
ws closed (reason=ready_send_failed)
... ~10 second gap ...
ws accepted peer=127.0.0.1:YYYYY
```

Additional warnings during runtime:
- `ws write slow (loop stalled >10.0s)` — WebSocket write stalls before disconnect
- `RuntimeError: Event loop is closed` — asyncio event loop closure in httpx backtrace
- `RuntimeError: Cannot call "send" once a close message has been sent.` — stale write attempts after close

## Log Evidence (errors.log)

- `UnicodeDecodeError: 'gbk' codec can't decode byte 0xa2 in position 5: illegal multibyte sequence` in gateway crash thread — a GBK encoding issue on Windows may be crashing a backend thread
- `config.yaml has empty section(s): context_file_max_chars, max_concurrent_sessions` — minor config warning

## Environment

- **OS**: Windows 10
- **App**: Hermes Desktop (Electron)
- **Provider**: DeepSeek / OpenRouter (both affected)
- **Desktop.log**: Shows multiple backend restart cycles with `[boot] Resolving Hermes backend` -> `HERMES_DASHBOARD_READY` -> back-end crash/restart

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Launch Hermes Desktop on Windows
2. Start a chat session
3. The UI begins flashing within minutes of use
4. Observe the WebSocket reconnect pattern in gui.log

## Expected Behavior

Stable WebSocket connection, no UI flickering. The chat box should stay responsive during normal use.

## Suggested Investigation

1. Check if the WebSocket heartbeat/keepalive is being handled correctly on Windows async I/O
2. Investigate the GBK `UnicodeDecodeError` in gateway thread — may be crashing the WS reader thread
3. Verify the Electron frontend handles WS reconnect gracefully without full re-render

## Platform

Windows 11, WSL2, Hermes Web Dashboard and Desktop app

## Description

Pasting Chinese/CJK text from the Windows clipboard into the Hermes Web Dashboard or Desktop app produces literal `???` instead of the actual characters.

Example: pasting `你好世界，测试中文` results in `????????????`.

## Root cause

The clipboard read path in `ui-tui/src/lib/clipboard.ts` uses `powershell.exe Get-Clipboard -Raw` with `-NoProfile`, which bypasses the user's PowerShell profile. PowerShell then outputs clipboard content using the system ANSI code page (CP936 on Chinese Windows), not UTF-8.

When Hermes reads with `encoding: 'utf8'`, it interprets ANSI-coded bytes as UTF-8, and bytes that don't form valid UTF-8 are replaced with `?`.

Affects ALL non-ASCII characters on non-UTF-8 Windows locales: CJK, emoji, accented characters (e, u, n), Cyrillic, etc.

## The fix already exists on the write path

In the same file (`clipboard.ts`), the **write** direction (lines 102-103) already solves the identical problem for `Set-Clipboard` using base64 + `UTF8.GetString`. But the **read** direction is still broken.

## Suggested fix

In `ui-tui/src/lib/clipboard.ts`, line 6, change:
```
const POWERSHELL_ARGS = ['-NoProfile', '-NonInteractive', '-Command', 'Get-Clipboard -Raw'] as const
```
to:
```
const POWERSHELL_ARGS = ['-NoProfile', '-NonInteractive', '-Command', '[Console]::OutputEncoding = [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8; Get-Clipboard -Raw'] as const
```

This forces PowerShell to use UTF-8 for stdout.

## Related issues

- #35107 - /copy in TUI produces garbled CJK text on WSL2 (same root cause, output direction)
- #38077 - Clipboard paste mangles emoji to ?? (same root cause)
- #43247 - Chinese IME not working on WSLg (separate IME issue)

labels.description: Web dashboard / control panel UI (dashboard/, landing)

items.body:
## Summary

Dashboard chat suffers from **three related WebSocket bugs** that together cause random loss of any part of the conversation (not only the last message):

1. **Token mismatch spam** — every `hermes dashboard` restart generates a new `_SESSION_TOKEN` in `web_server.py:264`. Existing TUI-Node children and SPA tabs hold the stale token and reconnect in a tight loop (~13 retries/minute), getting rejected with `pty auth rejected reason=token_mismatch`. Verified at **2130 rejections in 24h** vs only 180 successful `pty accepted` (8% success rate).
2. **No server-side replay buffer for PTY stream** — `pump_pty_to_ws` in `web_server.py:12227` sends each 200ms chunk directly via `ws.send_bytes(chunk)` with no buffering. On any WS close/reconnect/refresh, all chunks between disconnect and reconnect are lost.
3. **No client-side replay buffer for PTY stream either** — `ui-tui/dist/entry.js` `GatewayClient` has `bufferedEvents = new CircularBuffer(MAX_BUFFERED_EVENTS)`, but it covers only the JSON-RPC `/api/ws` metadata sidecar, NOT the `/api/pty` stream.

User-visible symptom: in any session, randomly either the beginning, the end, or a middle section of the conversation disappears, leaving only a fragment. Reproduces without any user action — happens mid-conversation in normal use.

This supersedes **#53700** which described only the "last message lost" symptom and proposed a SPA-side resync fix. That issue is closing because the root cause is broader (server-side PTY pipeline, not just SPA reconnect logic).

## Reproduction

### Token mismatch spam (deterministic)

1. Start `hermes dashboard` once: `hermes dashboard --no-open --port 9119`
2. Open `http://127.0.0.1:9119/` in browser, log in
3. Restart dashboard: from another shell, `systemctl --user restart hermes-gateway` (or `kill -TERM $(cat ~/.hermes/state/gateway.pid)`)
4. `tail -f ~/.hermes/logs/gui.log` — observe continuous:
   ```
   pty auth rejected reason=token_mismatch mode=loopback cred=token peer=127.0.0.1
   pty auth rejected reason=token_mismatch ...
   ```
   appearing ~13 times per minute until the browser tab is closed and reopened.

### Random loss of any part (probabilistic)

1. Open dashboard, start a chat session
2. Send a message that produces a long streamed response (≥30 seconds)
3. Mid-stream, force a WS disconnect via any of:
   - Browser DevTools → Network tab → right-click WS → "Close connection"
   - `chrome://net-internals/#sockets` → close the WS for 127.0.0.1:9119
   - `sudo tc qdisc add dev lo root netem loss 5%` (5% packet loss on loopback)
   - Brief network pause via `sudo iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 9119 -j DROP` for 2s then remove
4. After reconnect, observe that:
   - Sometimes the **last** assistant chunk is missing
   - Sometimes the **first** assistant chunk is missing
   - Sometimes a **middle** section is missing
   - Sometimes only a small fragment remains
5. F5 reload recovers all content (because it re-fetches from session store via the initial history load), confirming the data is in `state.db` — only the live stream lost it.

### Symptom categories (observed by user)

User has reported all three categories happening randomly in the same session, sometimes mid-conversation without any explicit WS drop:

| Symptom | User description |
|---|---|
| End of session gone | "конец сессии пропадает" — last chunk(s) of assistant's response missing from the rendered chat |
| Beginning gone | "начало исчезло" — opening message or first assistant response not visible |
| Middle gone | "основная часть сессии исчезает и остаётся небольшой кусок где-то в середине" — most of the conversation absent, only a small fragment remains |
| Random part in any session | "может случиться в рандомный момент в любой сессии" — no reproducible trigger from user's side |

Visual artifacts confirmed by user via screenshots:
- `Снимок экрана_20260628_062849.png` (1416×2508 portrait, 1.4 MB) — context: an earlier instance of the bug, full chat with missing section
- `Снимок экрана_20260628_065212.png` (3131×1340 landscape, 844 KB) — context: end-of-session disappearance in landscape layout

Note: vision tooling was unavailable at the time of reporting (`Auxiliary Nous client unavailable` in `~/.hermes/logs/errors.log` — `No LLM provider configured for task=vision provider=nous`). Symptom descriptions above are based on user's textual account, not automated image analysis.

## Root cause

### 1. Token mismatch

`~/.hermes/hermes-agent/hermes_cli/web_server.py:264`:

```python
_SESSION_TOKEN = os.environ.get("HERMES_DASHBOARD_SESSION_TOKEN") or secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
```

Every dashboard restart mints a new token. TUI-Node children spawn with the old token baked into their environment (`HERMES_TUI_SIDECAR_URL` etc.) and never refresh it. The SPA tab injects the old token via `__HERMES_SESSION_TOKEN__` in HTML and doesn't re-fetch on reconnect.

`hmac.compare_digest` at line 11806 rejects mismatched tokens with `close(code=4401, reason="auth: token_mismatch")`. The frontend has no special handling for 4401 — it just retries via the EventSource-style reconnect loop.

### 2. PTY stream has no replay buffer (the deep one)

`~/.hermes/hermes-agent/hermes_cli/web_server.py:12205-12227`:

```python
async def pump_pty_to_ws() -> None:
    try:
        await asyncio.wait_for(client_ready.wait(), timeout=2.0)
    except asyncio.TimeoutError:
        _log.info("pty pump ready_timeout peer=%s — streaming without client ack", peer)
    while True:
        chunk = await loop.run_in_executor(None, bridge.read, _PTY_READ_CHUNK_TIMEOUT)
        if chunk is None: return
        if not chunk:
            await asyncio.sleep(0); continue
        try:
            await ws.send_bytes(chunk)   # ← no buffer, no replay
        except Exception:
            return
```

A literal code comment in `web_server.py:12189-12197` acknowledges the race:

```python
# TUI starts streaming the moment PtyBridge.spawn returns.  On a brand-new
# WebSocket the browser's xterm.js is not yet wired to receive those bytes
# — the very first WS-handshake often races the first PTY chunk, and we
# have observed the gateway log exactly that pattern:
#     pty accepted peer=...
#     ws closed peer=... reason=client_disconnect(code=1005) messages=1
# i.e. the client reconnected before it had consumed any replay data,
# and the last assistant message in the previous frame disappeared.
```

The `client_ready.wait()` gate is partial — it only holds chunks for the first 2 seconds. After that, chunks flow unconditionally. On any later reconnect (browser tab sleep, network blip, gateway restart), nothing replays.

### 3. Client-side has no PTY buffer

`ui-tui/dist/entry.js` (3.8 MB minified) — `GatewayClient` has:

```js
bufferedEvents = new CircularBuffer(MAX_BUFFERED_EVENTS)
```

But grep for `binaryType`, `Uint8Array`, `.arrayBuffer()`, `/api/pty` in the bundle shows the PTY stream handler writes chunks directly into xterm.js with no buffering layer. Only the JSON-RPC sidecar (`/api/ws` for metadata) is buffered.

## Architecture gap (what's missing)

| Component | Present? | Location |
|---|---|---|
| Server-side replay buffer per PTY session | ❌ No | `web_server.py:12205-12227` sends each chunk directly |
| Resume handshake (client sends `lastSeenOffset` on reconnect) | ❌ No | `?resume=<session_id>` parameter exists at `pty_ws:12134` but only used for session history lookup, not for PTY stream replay |
| Client-side buffer for PTY stream | ❌ No | `entry.js` `GatewayClient.bufferedEvents` covers only metadata |
| Server flush of recent chunks on WS close | ⚠️ Partial | `web_server.py:12267-12270` sends only `\x1b[?25h\x1b[0m` ANSI terminator, not a replay of recent chunks |
| Token persistence between dashboard restarts | ❌ No | `_SESSION_TOKEN` regenerated every process start |

## Suggested fix (4 components)

### A. Persistent session token (`web_server.py:264`)

Store `_SESSION_TOKEN` in `~/.hermes/state/dashboard_session_token`. Read on startup, generate only if file is missing. Reused across restarts so TUI-Node children and SPA tabs keep working.

### B. Dedicated close code 4409 for stale token

Replace `close(code=4401, reason="auth: token_mismatch")` at line 12103 with `close(code=4409, reason="auth: token_mismatch")`. Reserve 4401 for other auth failures (no_credential, ticket_invalid). Clients can distinguish "stale token, please reload" from "credential missing/invalid".

### C. SPA frontend handler for 4409 (entry.js)

On `ws.close.code === 4409`:
1. If `localStorage.hermes:reloaded-once` is unset, set it and `location.reload()` (picks up new token from HTML)
2. If already reloaded once (token still mismatching), show actionable error instead of silently reconnecting in a loop

### D. Server-side ring buffer for PTY + resume handshake (web_server.py:12205 + entry.js)

`PtySessionBuffer` — circular buffer holding last 256KB of PTY output per `session_id`:

- `pump_pty_to_ws` writes each chunk **both** to `ws.send_bytes(chunk)` and to `PtySessionBuffer.append(session_id, chunk)`
- On reconnect with `?resume=<session_id>`, server sends the buffer contents **before** resuming the pump:
  ```
  Client                              Server
    |                                     |
    |-- WS upgrade /api/pty?resume=X ----->|
    |<-- first message: buffer replay -----|  (up to 256KB)
    |<-- regular PTY chunks ---------------|  (current stream)
  ```
- Extend `client_ready.wait()` from 2s to 5s, OR remove it entirely since the server-side buffer makes it unnecessary.

`?resume=<session_id>` is already parsed at `pty_ws:12134` (currently used for session metadata lookup); extend it to also trigger PTY buffer replay.

### Optional E. Client-side PTY buffer (entry.js)

Add a second `CircularBuffer` for PTY chunks in `GatewayClient` (64KB). On WS reconnect, client can include `lastSeenOffset` to request replay from a specific point. Lower priority than server-side — server has authoritative buffer; client buffer is just defense-in-depth.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent `0.17.0` (upstream `163cb24d`)
- Python 3.13.13 (venv at `~/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv`)
- Dashboard served at `127.0.0.1:9119`
- Browser: Chromium-based, single tab, no extensions
- Affects: embedded chat tab (`/chat`) and the desktop app's Chat tab
- Verified on CachyOS Linux 7.1.1-2, KDE Plasma 6.7.1, Wayland

## Observed log statistics (24h, 2026-06-27 → 2026-06-28)

| Metric | Count |
|---|---|
| `pty accepted` (successful) | 180 |
| `pty auth rejected reason=token_mismatch` | **2130** |
| `ws closed code=1005` (no close frame, client died) | 214 |
| `ws closed code=1001` (going away) | 103 |
| `ws closed code=1012` (server restart) | 15 |
| `ws send failed` (race on close) | 6 |
| `ws response send failed` | 5 |
| **Success-to-rejection ratio for PTY connections** | **1:11.8** |

Token mismatch burst pattern from real restart at 2026-06-27 19:51:

```
19:51:25.792  ws accepted peer=127.0.0.1:32964
19:51:25.825  pty accepted peer=127.0.0.1 mode=loopback cred=token
19:51:40.782-788  ws closed code=1012 (server restart)
19:51:42.327  Mounted plugin API routes           ← dashboard reboot
19:51:42.867  pty auth rejected reason=token_mismatch
19:51:43.037  pty auth rejected reason=token_mismatch
19:51:44.885  pty auth rejected reason=token_mismatch
…continues at ~13/min until browser tab is closed
```

## Severity

**P2 (medium-high)** — was P3 in #53700, but the broader symptom (random loss of any part, not just last message; ~92% PTY connection rejection rate after restart) elevates this. Not data-loss-critical (state.db is authoritative), but UX-fatal for the dashboard chat surface — every long conversation has chunks missing, and F5 is the only recovery.

## Workaround for users (while this is unfixed)

1. **Token mismatch spam**: close the browser tab completely and reopen — fresh HTML injects new `_SESSION_TOKEN`. This stops the spam immediately.
2. **Random chunk loss**: F5 reload — re-fetches full history from session store, recovering all content. State.db is authoritative; only the live UI drops chunks.

items.title: [Bug]: TUI drops Vietnamese tone marks — IME backspace+char batched in one stdin read is silently discarded
items.body:
### Bug Description

Typing Vietnamese in the **TUI** (`comp/tui`) silently drops tone marks and mangles syllables. Intending to type `tôi gõ tiếng Việt vậy rồi` produces something like `to i go tien g iếng Vie t vay ro i` — tone/circumflex marks are eaten and stray spaces appear mid-syllable.

This is **terminal-independent**: it reproduces even in Apple Terminal, where the `"\b \b"` fast-echo bypass is already disabled. So this is NOT the fast-echo path — the defect is in keypress parsing, upstream of the composer.

Note: this is the **TUI counterpart** of the Desktop composer bug #39636 (Vietnamese Telex). The Desktop fix does not cover the TUI, which has a separate input pipeline (`ui-tui/` + `hermes-ink`).

### Steps to Reproduce

1. macOS, use a third-party Vietnamese IME that recomposes via backspace (OpenKey / Unikey / EVKey), Telex mode.
2. Launch the TUI (`hermes` / `hermes chat`) — reproduces in Apple Terminal too, not just Warp.
3. In the composer, type a Vietnamese sentence, e.g. `tôi gõ tiếng Việt vậy rồi` (Telex keystrokes: `tooi gox tiengs Vieet vaay rooif`).
4. Observe the committed draft: tone marks dropped, characters lost, stray spaces inserted mid-syllable.

### Expected Behavior

Vietnamese input commits with correct diacritics, yielding `tôi gõ tiếng Việt vậy rồi`. When the IME recomposes a syllable by emitting a backspace immediately followed by the finished character (in the same stdin read), the backspace should delete the half-formed letter and the new character should be inserted.

### Actual Behavior

Tone marks are dropped, characters are lost, and stray spaces appear mid-syllable. The recomposed character (with its tone mark) never reaches the composer.

Observed at the parser level (codepoints explicit):

```
input "\x7fô"  (U+007F U+00F4)        => 1 key  { name: "",  sequence: [U+007F U+00F4] }
input "\x7fôi" (U+007F U+00F4 U+0069) => 1 key  { name: "",  sequence: [U+007F U+00F4 U+0069] }
```

A chunk that mixes a DEL (0x7f) with the following character parses to `name: ""` with a non-printable sequence, which the composer then discards.

### Affected Component

CLI (interactive chat)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
(Filing from a browser, so `hermes debug share` output isn't attached here — happy to run it and paste the links if needed.)

Manual environment summary:
- Hermes Desktop / TUI build observed: ~v0.17.x (TUI runs from `~/.hermes/hermes-agent/ui-tui/dist/entry.js`)
- OS: macOS 26.5.1 (also seen on macOS 15.x)
- Terminals reproduced in: Apple Terminal and Warp
- IME: third-party Vietnamese (OpenKey), Telex mode
- Component: TUI input pipeline (`ui-tui/` + `packages/hermes-ink`)
```

### Operating System

macOS 26.5.1 (also reproduced on macOS 15.x); reproduces in Apple Terminal and Warp

### Python Version

_No response_

### Hermes Version

Hermes Agent v0.17.0 (TUI)

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

**Note: this is a confirmed parser-level defect, but it may NOT be the complete root cause** — a patch I tried based solely on it did not fully fix real typing in the TUI, so there is likely an additional issue (e.g. the IME may emit a different byte sequence than assumed, or send separate per-keystroke reads). Sharing what I verified so far as a lead:

Pipeline: `ui-tui/packages/hermes-ink/src/ink/parse-keypress.ts` → `ui-tui/src/components/textInput.tsx`.

Verified directly against `parseMultipleKeypresses` (codepoints explicit):

```
input "\x7fô"  (U+007F U+00F4)        => 1 key  { name: "",  sequence: [U+007F U+00F4] }      -> dropped
input "\x7fôi" (U+007F U+00F4 U+0069) => 1 key  { name: "",  sequence: [U+007F U+00F4 U+0069] } -> dropped
```

Chain for this particular defect:
1. A third-party Vietnamese IME (OpenKey/Unikey/EVKey) recomposes a syllable by erasing the half-formed letter and re-emitting the finished one. In at least some cases a single stdin read arrives as DEL (`0x7f`) immediately followed by the composed character(s), e.g. `\x7fô`.
2. The tokenizer (`termio/tokenize.ts`) keeps `0x7f` inside one **text** token `"\x7fô"`.
3. `parseMultipleKeypresses` passes the whole text token to `parseKeypress(token.value)`, which only matches backspace on an **exact** `s === "\x7f"` / `s === "\b"`. So `"\x7fô"` falls through every branch and returns `name: ""` with `sequence: "\x7fô"`.
4. In `textInput.tsx`, `name` is empty so it is not treated as backspace; it goes to the insert path, where `PRINTABLE = /^[ -~\u00a0-\uffff]+$/` fails on the leading `0x7f`, so `applyPrintableInsert(...)` returns `null` and the handler `return`s — the chunk is dropped.

This path is independent of the `supportsFastEchoTerminal` denylist, consistent with the bug reproducing in Apple Terminal (fast-echo already off). Please treat it as a lead rather than the definitive cause — fixing only this did not fully resolve typing in my testing.

items.title: [Feature]: Webhook-triggered sessions need a cron_mode-equivalent exemption from gateway approval waits

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

items.body:
## Problem

`_is_gateway_approval_context()` in `tools/approval.py` deliberately excludes cron sessions from the blocking gateway-approval branch, with this rationale in the function's own docstring:

> "Cron jobs are NEVER gateway-approval contexts even when they originate from a gateway platform (cron binds HERMES_SESSION_PLATFORM via contextvars for delivery routing). Cron approvals are governed by `approvals.cron_mode` config, not interactive resolve — letting cron fall through to the gateway branch would submit a pending approval with no listener and block the job indefinitely."

Webhook-triggered sessions (the `webhook` platform adapter, e.g. a job-tracker/ticketing system waking the agent via `task.assigned`) hit exactly the scenario this docstring describes, but are not given the same exemption. `_is_gateway_approval_context()` returns `True` for `HERMES_SESSION_PLATFORM=webhook` sessions, so any dangerous-pattern command that the `smart` approval mode escalates (verdict `escalate`, i.e. the auxiliary LLM is uncertain) falls into the blocking `_await_gateway_decision()` path with a 300s timeout — even though, like cron, there is no human listening on a webhook-triggered unattended session.

## Impact (observed in production use)

A webhook-triggered session working a multi-step infra task hit a command that escalated to the manual-wait branch. It waited the full 300s, got silence (no listener), received the standard `BLOCKED: ... Do NOT retry ...` message, but the underlying agent loop made another tool call anyway a few turns later (LLM didn't fully internalize the "stop" instruction), hit the *same* wait again, and repeated this multiple times across a single turn, each consuming ~5 minutes and contributing to the session exhausting its `max_iterations` budget before completing the actual task. Reproduced with `approvals.mode: smart` (which mostly avoids this since `approve`/`deny` verdicts skip the wait entirely) — the gap is specifically the `escalate` verdict path, which still funnels into the same gateway-wait branch regardless of platform.

## Suggested fix

Add a `webhook_mode` config key under `approvals:`, mirroring `cron_mode` (`approve` | `deny`, same semantics), and have `_is_gateway_approval_context()` (or its caller) treat `HERMES_SESSION_PLATFORM=webhook` the same way it already treats `HERMES_CRON_SESSION` — i.e. webhook sessions should be governed by `approvals.webhook_mode`, not fall through to the interactive/gateway-wait branch. This is a small, mechanical extension of a pattern that's already implemented and documented for cron; webhook-triggered automation has the identical "no listener present" property.

## Environment

- hermes-agent installed via the standard installer, custom OpenAI-compatible provider (non-OAuth)
- `approvals.mode: smart`, `approvals.cron_mode: auto`
- Triggered via the bundled `webhook` platform adapter (dynamic subscription, `task.assigned` event)

Happy to provide the exact command pattern that escalated and full session logs if useful — kept this report at the architecture level since the underlying issue (missing webhook exemption) generalizes beyond the specific command.

items.body:
## Bug / reliability issue

For at least one Photon/Spectrum shared-number iMessage project, the live inbound stream remained cold even while the unary message history API could see inbound messages. This made the gateway appear connected, but inbound iMessages did not reliably reach Hermes unless a polling fallback was added.

## Symptoms observed

- Photon sidecar/gateway reported connected.
- Outbound send worked.
- Inbound live stream did not deliver new messages.
- `@photon-ai/advanced-imessage` history/listing calls could see the messages.
- Adding a narrow polling fallback for configured/allowed DMs made inbound delivery reliable.

## Expected

If Photon reports connected and the configured iMessage line receives a DM from an allowed sender, the sidecar should deliver that inbound event to the Hermes gateway.

## Actual

The stream path can remain cold for shared-number projects, so the gateway stays apparently healthy but inbound delivery is missing.

## Local mitigation verified

A narrow fallback loop worked locally:

- derive poll targets from `PHOTON_HOME_CHANNEL` / `PHOTON_ALLOWED_USERS`
- issue shared iMessage tokens via `@spectrum-ts/core`
- use `@photon-ai/advanced-imessage` `messages.listInChat(...)`
- normalize new non-`isFromMe` messages into the same inbound event shape
- dedupe by message `guid`/`id`
- keep the existing live stream; polling is only a fallback/overlap-safe path

Local sidecar logs after mitigation:

```text
photon-sidecar: poll fallback enabled for 1 target(s)
✓ photon connected
Gateway running with 1 platform(s)
```

And inbound messages were delivered again.

## Notes

This may only affect shared-number/free-tier Photon projects or specific token/stream states. It would be useful for the sidecar to either:

1. expose a health signal distinguishing "connected but stream cold" from actually receiving events, or
2. include an opt-in bounded polling fallback for configured/allowed DMs.

## Environment

- Hermes git install from `NousResearch/hermes-agent`
- Photon iMessage plugin/sidecar
- Shared-number Photon/Spectrum path
- Linux gateway host

items.title: [Bug]: TUI /reasoning and /fast mutate global config instead of session-scoped overrides
items.body:
## Summary

In the TUI, `/reasoning <level>` and `/fast <mode>` update the live agent, but they also persist the change to `~/.hermes/config.yaml`.

This makes quick per-task switches unsafe: after using high reasoning or fast mode for one task, future sessions inherit that setting unless the user manually switches back.

This appears inconsistent with gateway `/reasoning`, which was changed after #9586 to be session-scoped by default and only persist with `--global`.

## Current behavior

In TUI:

```text
/reasoning high
```

writes:

```yaml
agent:
  reasoning_effort: high
```

and:

```text
/fast fast
```

writes:

```yaml
agent:
  service_tier: fast
```

So the change survives new sessions and affects unrelated work.

## Expected behavior

TUI should mirror gateway semantics:

```text
/reasoning high          # current TUI session only
/reasoning high --global # persist to config.yaml
/reasoning reset         # clear session override, fall back to global config

/fast fast               # current TUI session only
/fast fast --global      # persist to config.yaml
/fast reset              # clear session override, fall back to global config
```

## Why this matters

Reasoning effort and fast mode are frequently task-local choices:

- low/minimal for quick edits or lookups
- high/xhigh for deep debugging or planning
- fast for urgent turns
- normal for cost/control

Persisting these by default is easy to forget and can silently increase cost or latency across future sessions.

## Related issues

- #9586: requested session-only `/reasoning`; gateway now appears to implement this semantic.
- #40890: requests one-shot reasoning control for `hermes chat -q`.
- #50449: another TUI/Desktop `config.set reasoning` path bug.
- #51754: keyboard-first users want slash command access for `/reasoning` and `/fast` in Desktop.

## Likely root cause

TUI slash command frontend calls:

```ts
config.set { key: "reasoning", value: arg }
config.set { key: "fast", value: mode }
```

The TUI gateway backend handles these by writing global config:

```python
_write_config_key("agent.reasoning_effort", arg)
_write_config_key("agent.service_tier", nv)
```

It then updates the live agent, so the command works immediately, but it also leaks into the global profile default.

## Suggested fix

Make TUI `config.set reasoning` and `config.set fast` session-scoped by default.

For `/reasoning`:

- parse `--global` / `--session` or equivalent
- default to session override
- update `session["agent"].reasoning_config`
- persist via session runtime metadata, not `config.yaml`
- only write `agent.reasoning_effort` when `--global` is passed
- support `reset` to remove the session override

For `/fast`:

- same default session-only semantics
- update `agent.service_tier` and `agent.request_overrides`
- persist via session runtime metadata
- only write `agent.service_tier` when `--global` is passed
- support `reset`

TUI already has session runtime persistence helpers such as `_persist_live_session_runtime()`, and session creation already carries `create_reasoning_override` / `create_service_tier_override`, so this should be a parity fix rather than a new feature.

items.title: [Docs]: SearXNG configuration instructions are outdated
items.body:
The current SearXNG setup guide instructs users to edit an existing top-level formats block in `settings.yml`:

```yml
formats:
  - html
```

However, recent versions of SearXNG generate a minimal settings.yml when use_default_settings: true is enabled (the default). The file only contains configuration overrides, so the formats block does not exist.
As a result, users following the guide cannot find the configuration section being referenced.

To enable JSON responses, the documentation should instead instruct users to add the following override:

```yml
search:
  formats:
    - html
    - json
```

This reflects how SearXNG's configuration inheritance works and matches the current default configuration layout.

items.body:
## Bug Description

When the `model.default` in `config.yaml` uses `anthropic_messages` mode (e.g. `minimax-m3` on `opencode-go`) and the user invokes `hermes chat -m <chat_completions_model> -q "..."`, the CLI does **not** re-derive `self.api_mode` or `self.base_url` for the requested model. It keeps the `api_mode=anthropic_messages` and `base_url=https://opencode.ai/zen/go` (without `/v1`) from the config default, and all calls to non-MiniMax models fail with **HTTP 404** (the "Not Found" HTML page from opencode.ai).

## Steps to Reproduce

**Config:**
```yaml
model:
  default: minimax-m3
  provider: opencode-go
```

**Env:**
```
OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY=sk-...
```

**Failing command:**
```bash
hermes chat -m qwen3.7-plus -q "ok"
# → HTTP 404 — Not Found | opencode
```

**Working workaround:**
```bash
hermes config set model.default qwen3.7-plus
hermes chat -q "ok"   # ✅
```

## Expected Behavior

`hermes chat -m qwen3.7-plus` should derive `api_mode=chat_completions` and `base_url=https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1` for `qwen3.7-plus`, regardless of what `model.default` is set to.

## Actual Behavior

The CLI uses the api_mode/base_url derived from `model.default` (`minimax-m3` → `anthropic_messages`, `base_url` without `/v1`). The OpenAI SDK constructs `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/chat/completions` → **404**.

Only `minimax-m3` works, by coincidence: its `api_mode=anthropic_messages` matches the default, and the Anthropic SDK constructs `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/messages`, which exists.

## Root Cause

`_ensure_runtime_credentials()` in `hermes_cli/cli_agent_setup_mixin.py` (lines 41-45) calls `resolve_runtime_provider(requested=self.requested_provider, ...)` **without passing `target_model`**. The resolver then falls back to `model_cfg.get("default")` to derive `api_mode`, picking the wrong mode for any model that differs from the config default.

`resolve_runtime_provider` already accepts a `target_model` kwarg (added in #16878 / PR #16890 for the `/model` switch path) — it just isn't being passed here.

### Evidence with `curl`

```bash
# Correct endpoint (with /v1) → works
curl -X POST https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"qwen3.7-plus","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"ok"}]}'
# → HTTP 200, valid response

# Endpoint Hermes uses (without /v1) → 404 HTML
curl -X POST https://opencode.ai/zen/go/chat/completions ...
# → HTTP 404, "Not Found | opencode" HTML page
```

### Evidence with `resolve_runtime_provider` in isolation

```python
# With target_model (what the fix does):
resolve_runtime_provider(requested="opencode-go", target_model="qwen3.7-plus")
# → api_mode="chat_completions", base_url="https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1" ✅

# Without target_model (current CLI behavior):
resolve_runtime_provider(requested="opencode-go")
# → api_mode="anthropic_messages", base_url="https://opencode.ai/zen/go" ❌
```

## Environment

- **Hermes Agent:** v0.17.0, commit `caf4dcc7a`
- **Provider:** opencode-go (OpenCode Go subscription)
- **OS:** Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, Python 3.11.15
- **Catalog:** 20 models available on opencode-go; only `minimax-m3` works with `-m`, all other 19 fail with 404

## Related Issues

- **#16878** — same bug family, fixed the `/model` switch path but not the CLI single-query (`-m`) path.
- **#15319** — same root cause in `delegate_tool.py` (missing `target_model`), fixed with the same one-line pattern.
- **#53251** — complementary fix for `runtime_override` staleness in `_init_agent` (openai-codex); compatible with the fix for this issue.

items.title: Bug: Stale Telegram bot token lock permanently kills platform (retryable=False in _acquire_platform_lock)

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Summary

When a Hermes gateway process is killed (SIGKILL, crash, SIGTERM) during Telegram initialization, the scoped lock file (`~/.local/state/hermes/gateway-locks/telegram-bot-token-*.lock`) survives. On next startup, `_acquire_platform_lock()` in `gateway/platforms/base.py` detects the conflict and calls `_set_fatal_error(..., retryable=False)`, which **permanently kills the Telegram platform** — even when the owning PID is confirmed dead.

## Root Cause

The `acquire_scoped_lock()` function in `gateway/status.py` (line 882+) correctly:
1. Reads the existing lock file
2. Checks if the PID is alive via `_pid_exists()`
3. Detects stale locks and deletes the file

However, when the lock is stale, it **still returns `(False, existing_dict)`** to the caller. The caller `_acquire_platform_lock()` in `base.py:2557` sees `acquired=False` and unconditionally calls:

```python
self._set_fatal_error(f'{scope}_lock', message, retryable=False)
```

This permanently marks Telegram as dead. The reconnect watcher never retries because `retryable=False`.

## Reproduction

1. Start Hermes gateway with Telegram configured
2. Force-kill the gateway process (`kill -9 <PID>`) before Telegram finishes initializing
3. Restart the gateway
4. Log shows: `[Telegram] Telegram bot token already in use (PID XXXXX). Stop the other gateway first.`
5. Telegram stays disconnected forever until manual intervention

## Evidence

Multiple incidents observed in production:
- 2026-06-23: PID 9882 stale lock, Telegram permanently dead
- 2026-06-28: PID 25361 stale lock, Telegram permanently dead (confirmed dead via `kill -0`)

## Proposed Fix

Change `base.py:2557` from:
```python
self._set_fatal_error(f'{scope}_lock', message, retryable=False)
```
to:
```python
self._set_fatal_error(f'{scope}_lock', message, retryable=True)
```

With `retryable=True`:
1. Stale lock is detected and deleted by `acquire_scoped_lock()`
2. Platform is queued for background reconnection (30s delay)
3. On retry, lock file is gone → `_acquire_platform_lock()` succeeds → Telegram connects

## Impact

- **Severity:** High — Telegram becomes permanently unusable until manual intervention
- **Affected platforms:** Telegram (the only platform using scoped lock for bot token)
- **Frequency:** Occurs after any abrupt gateway termination (crash, kill -9, force-quit)
- **Workaround:** Manual deletion of lock file + gateway restart

# [Windows] terminal tool hangs when launching GUI programs via .exe or start command

## Environment
- **Hermes Agent version:** latest (main branch)
- **OS:** Windows 10
- **Shell:** MSYS/Git Bash (the default for Hermes on Windows)
- **Desktop App:** Yes (Hermes Desktop GUI)

## Problem

On Windows, running any GUI .exe program through the `terminal` tool causes the session to hang indefinitely.

**Affected commands (all hang):**
```bash
# Direct .exe execution — hangs
"C:\path\to\program.exe"
# Windows start command in MSYS bash — also hangs
start "" "C:\path\to\program.exe"
# With timeout parameter — still hangs
terminal(command="program.exe", timeout=5)
```

## Root Cause

Hermes runs terminal commands in MSYS (Git Bash) on Windows. When a GUI .exe is launched:
1. bash forks the process and waits for it to exit — GUI programs don't exit → hang forever
2. `start` command has path conversion issues in MSYS and still blocks
3. `timeout=N` only limits execution time but doesn't kill the child GUI process

## Workaround (Proven)

Using PowerShell's Start-Process works because PowerShell exits immediately:

```bash
# Works — returns immediately
powershell -Command "Start-Process 'C:\path\to\program.exe'"
```

## Suggested Fixes

1. **Documentation:** Add a note about Windows GUI programs in terminal tool docs
2. **Tool improvement:** Auto-wrap .exe execution with PowerShell on Windows
3. **Timeout enforcement:** Actually kill child processes when timeout is exceeded

## Impact

Affects any workflow needing to launch GUI programs on Windows — download managers, VPN clients, IDEs, etc.

items.body:
### Summary

`hermes -z` (oneshot) against Anthropic via the auto-seeded `claude_code` OAuth
pool credential sends the request to the **wrong endpoint with an empty token**,
even though provider resolution and `AIAgent` initialization are both correct.

The outgoing request is built as **`POST https://api.anthropic.com/chat/completions`**
with **`Authorization: Bearer None`** (header length 11), instead of
`POST /v1/messages` with the OAuth bearer token. The server returns
`400 invalid_request_error`, and the user only sees:

```text
hermes -z: no final response was produced; treating the run as failed.
```

The same account works fine through `hermes chat` / the gateway (which go through
`HermesCLI._init_agent()`); only the oneshot path is affected.

This is distinct from #45155 (which was a *real* low-balance billing error being
hidden). Here there is **no real billing problem** — the request never carries a
valid token or the native Anthropic api_mode, so the 400 is a symptom of a
credential/api_mode loss at request-build time, not an account issue.

### Environment

- Hermes: `0.17.0`
- Platform: macOS
- Python: `3.11`
- Provider: `anthropic`, default model `claude-opus-4-8`
- Auth: auto-seeded `claude_code` pool credential (OAuth token borrowed from
  `~/.claude/.credentials.json`); `auth.json` has `active_provider: anthropic`
  and **no** explicit anthropic credential entry (token comes purely from the
  pool/keychain seed).

### Reproduction

```sh
hermes -z "Reply with exactly: PONG"
# -> hermes -z: no final response was produced; treating the run as failed.  (exit 1)
```

Inspect the newest request dump:

```sh
ls -t ~/.hermes/sessions/request_dump_*.json | head -1
```

It shows:

```json
{
  "reason": "non_retryable_client_error",
  "request": {
    "url": "https://api.anthropic.com/chat/completions",
    "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer None", "Content-Type": "application/json" },
    "body": { "model": "claude-opus-4-8", ... }
  },
  "error": { "type": "invalid_request_error",
             "message": "Error code: 400 - ... You're out of extra usage ..." }
}
```

(Across the last 15 dumps: `reason=non_retryable_client_error` and
`url=.../chat/completions` every time.)

### Diagnosis — root cause is in the oneshot request path, NOT in resolution or init

I instrumented the real oneshot code path (`hermes_cli/oneshot.py::_run_agent`)
using the project venv. Everything up to and including `AIAgent.__init__` is
**correct**; the failure appears only when the request is actually built inside
`agent.chat()`.

**1. `resolve_runtime_provider` resolves correctly** — both with explicit args and
with the exact args oneshot uses (`requested=None, target_model=None`):

```text
provider : anthropic
api_mode : anthropic_messages
api_key  : <set len=108>
base_url : https://api.anthropic.com
cred_pool: CredentialPool
```

**2. The CredentialPool is healthy** — `select()`/`current()`/`peek()` all return
the valid credential:

```text
PooledCredential(provider='anthropic', id='524a64', label='claude_code', auth_ty...)
```

**3. `AIAgent` receives and stores everything correctly.** Spying on
`run_agent.AIAgent` during `_run_agent(...)`:

```text
--- AIAgent receives (before super) ---
provider : anthropic
api_mode : anthropic_messages
api_key  : <set len=108>
base_url : https://api.anthropic.com
cred_pool: CredentialPool
--- AIAgent after init (effective) ---
eff provider : anthropic
eff api_mode : anthropic_messages
eff base_url : https://api.anthropic.com
```

So `agent_init.py` is fine (and even the fallback at
`agent_init.py:332` would set `anthropic_messages` for `provider == "anthropic"`).

**Conclusion:** despite a correct `api_mode=anthropic_messages` and a healthy
CredentialPool on the agent, the request emitted by `agent.chat()` in the
oneshot context is built as `chat_completions` + `Bearer None`. The api_mode
and/or the pool-resolved token are lost/ignored at request-build time on the
oneshot path specifically. Suspected area: the transport/credential-acquisition
step in `agent.chat()` reads a per-request key (e.g. via the credential pool
lease) that comes back empty in the oneshot context, and the transport defaults
to the chat_completions adapter when the bearer is empty — whereas the
`_init_agent` path (gateway / `hermes chat`) does not hit this.

### Expected

`hermes -z` should emit `POST /v1/messages` with the OAuth bearer token (i.e. use
the already-resolved `api_mode=anthropic_messages` and the pool credential),
exactly like `hermes chat` / the gateway, and return a normal response.

### Additional / related

- The user-facing error also hides the real provider response (overlaps with
  #45155). Surfacing the actual HTTP status + provider message in the oneshot
  failure would have made this far faster to diagnose.
- Workaround until fixed: use `hermes chat` / the gateway instead of `hermes -z`
  for Anthropic with the `claude_code` OAuth pool credential.

# [Tracking] Windows Desktop GUI: console windows (cmd / conhost / git / gh / powershell) flash on subprocess spawns

cc @emozilla @OutThisLife

This is the umbrella tracking issue for the most-reported active bug on the repo: on the **Windows desktop GUI app**, black console windows flash on screen — sometimes continuously — whenever a child process is spawned. This issue consolidates **~25 open reports**, documents the **fix attempts we tried and reverted**, the **resolved history**, and — most importantly — a **forensic, code-verified map of which spawn sites are still leaking on current `main`** so the next fix targets the real cause instead of another red herring.

All findings below were verified by reading the actual source on current `main` (`9d919daf4`) and the git history — not by trusting reporter hypotheses.

---

## ◆ The mechanism (verified, not assumed)

The desktop GUI runs its Python backend headless via **`pythonw.exe`** (no console). When a windowless parent (`pythonw.exe`, or Electron itself) spawns a **console-subsystem child** (`cmd.exe`, `git.exe`, `gh.exe`, `wmic`, `powershell.exe`, `bash.exe`, `node.exe`, `uv.exe`) **without** the no-window flag, Windows allocates a fresh `conhost.exe` / `OpenConsole.exe` for that child and it flashes on screen.

The fix primitive **already exists** and is correct:
- **Python:** `hermes_cli/_subprocess_compat.py` → `windows_hide_flags()` returns `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` (0x08000000); `windows_detach_flags()` adds `DETACHED_PROCESS | CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP | CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB` for daemons.
- **Electron:** `apps/desktop/electron/main.cjs` → `hiddenWindowsChildOptions()` adds `windowsHide: true`.

The bug is **inconsistent application** of these helpers across the dozens of subprocess call sites — plus **two complications** the flag alone does not solve (see Caveats).

---

## ⚠ Red herrings & what we already tried (READ THIS FIRST)

We have burned real cycles here. Do not repeat these.

### The reverted cluster (June 27 2026)
Three PRs were merged and **all reverted the same day** via #53853 (`d3d621f7c`):

| PR | Commit | What it did |
|---|---|---|
| #53791 (@teknium1) | `ef17cd204` | AST footgun subprocess rule + 62-site sweep + CI guard + tests |
| #53810 (@OutThisLife) | `5db1430af` | `_subprocess_compat.run/popen` wrappers + `FreeConsole` catch-all + `test_no_visible_console_spawns.py` |
| #53829 (@teknium1) | `2ecca1e7d` | "capture is not a no-window boundary" chokepoint migration (35 sites) |

**Why they were reverted (from the revert PR body, the authoritative statement):** all four chased the wrong layer — `subprocess.*` call sites reasoned about on Linux — while the actual `hermes update → gateway restart` flash lives elsewhere in the spawn chain (the gateway-restart watcher launched via `sys.executable`, `.bat`/VBS launchers, the uv `python.exe` re-exec, or the Electron desktop relaunch). **The AST footgun checker is a call-site denylist that structurally cannot see those, so CI went green while the popup persisted. None of the four were ever run on native Windows.**

→ The CI guard (`test_no_visible_console_spawns.py` + the footgun *subprocess* rule) is **gone** from `main` as of the revert. The pre-existing footgun rules (os.kill / signal / wmic / powershell) remain.

### Other rejected/superseded approaches
- **`pythonw.exe` re-exec shim is not enough** (#52239 `d430684d7`): a venv `python.exe` is a launcher shim that re-execs the **base console interpreter**, which allocates its **own** conhost — and `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` cannot suppress that second window. Fix was to rewrite the respawn argv to `pythonw.exe` directly.
- **#44288** (base pythonw for post-update respawn) — closed, superseded by #52239.
- **#45453** (CREATE_NO_WINDOW on uv calls) — closed, never merged.

### ✔ Already suppressed (do not "fix" these — many stale reports point here)
| Site | Flag |
|---|---|
| `tools/environments/local.py:835` — **terminal() tool bash spawn** | `windows_hide_flags()` |

The flashes those users still see come from the **auxiliary probe/scan/launcher legs below**, or from the two OS-level complications.

### ❌ STILL MISSING the flag on current `main` (the real candidate root causes)

Highest-frequency first — these fire inside the `pythonw.exe` desktop backend, repeatedly, every session/turn:

1. **`tui_gateway/git_probe.py:49`** (`run_git`) — dashboard **Projects-tree** scanner. 1. **Windows 11 Default Terminal = Windows Terminal** intercepts console-subsystem spawns at the OS level and can override `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` (#24073, #53178). 2. **Electron Job Object** can block `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` on detached children; needs `CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB` with an `ACCESS_DENIED` fallback (#53273) — already handled for the gateway watcher (#40909) but relevant if new detached spawns are added.

**Group A — terminal/bash conhost per command:** #42544, #49851, #52310, #53014, #53273, #52788, #43848, #24073
**Group B — gateway/dashboard background scans (git/wmic):** #53178, #53424, #49602, #53631

2. **Fix `git_probe.py` encoding** (`encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"`) for CJK paths in the same pass.

4. **Reinstate a CI guard that works** — the reverted AST denylist couldn't see the real legs. Prefer a runtime/integration check that actually exercises the spawn chain, not a static call-site scan.
